report_name: APT28 (Forest Blizzard) Uses DNS Poisoning in 'FrostArmada' Campaign

threat_actors.name: Forest Blizzard
threat_actors.description: A Russian GRU state-sponsored threat group that conducted the 'FrostArmada' cyberespionage campaign. The group compromised gateway routers in hospitality environments to perform DNS poisoning, intercept traffic, and steal Microsoft credentials and OAuth tokens.
threat_actors.goals: To gather intelligence by stealing credentials and OAuth tokens to gain long-term access to corporate email, cloud storage, and other sensitive resources from government, military, and security organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: The attackers established a Man-in-the-Middle position by modifying DNS settings on compromised gateway routers to poison DNS responses. This redirected users to a phishing server when they tried to access legitimate sites like login.microsoftonline.com.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Used to gain initial access to edge network devices, specifically gateway routers in hospitality locations, by exploiting vulnerabilities or using weak credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The attackers intercepted and stole OAuth access tokens from users via their phishing infrastructure, providing persistent access to the victims' cloud applications.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The campaign's goal was to use the stolen credentials and OAuth tokens to gain access to a wide array of corporate accounts for intelligence gathering purposes.

campaigns.name: FrostArmada
campaigns.description: A cyberespionage campaign attributed to Forest Blizzard (APT28) that compromised gateway routers in hospitality Wi-Fi networks to conduct DNS poisoning and steal Microsoft credentials and OAuth tokens.
campaigns.objective: Credential and OAuth token harvesting for corporate espionage.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: The technology company whose login page (login.microsoftonline.com) was impersonated by the attackers' phishing server to harvest credentials and OAuth tokens.

identities.name: Hospitality Sector
identities.description: The industry sector, including hotels and conference centers, whose network gateway routers were compromised to facilitate the DNS poisoning attacks.

identities.name: Government Organizations
identities.description: A primary target vertical for the FrostArmada campaign's intelligence gathering objectives.

identities.name: Military Organizations
identities.description: A primary target vertical for the FrostArmada campaign's intelligence gathering objectives.

identities.name: Technology Organizations
identities.description: A target vertical for the FrostArmada campaign's intelligence gathering objectives.

identities.name: Financial Organizations
identities.description: A target vertical for the FrostArmada campaign's intelligence gathering objectives.

infrastructure.name: Malicious DNS Server
infrastructure.description: An attacker-controlled DNS server used to provide malicious IP addresses in response to DNS queries for legitimate services, redirecting victims to a phishing site.

infrastructure.name: Microsoft Login Phishing Server
infrastructure.description: An attacker-controlled server hosting a clone of the Microsoft login page to harvest user credentials and OAuth tokens.

indicators.name: Anomalous M365 Logins from Public Wi-Fi
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous M365 Logins from Public Wi-Fi
id: 7c5d1e8a-4b3f-4e9a-8f0c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects successful Microsoft 365 sign-ins from IP addresses associated with public Wi-Fi or hospitality networks, which could indicate credential theft from campaigns like FrostArmada that target travelers.
references:
  - https://www.technewsworld.com/story/dns-poisoning-campaign-makes-hospitality-wi-fi-spots-inhospitable-180463.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-29
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.initial_access
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user logins while traveling. This rule is intended to flag activity for correlation with travel schedules and other context.
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: 0
    AppDisplayName|contains:
      - 'Office 365'
      - 'Microsoft Office'
  filter_corporate_net:
    IPAddress|cidr:
      # Add your corporate IP ranges here
      - '192.0.2.0/24'
  condition: selection and not filter_corporate_net
indicators.description: Detects successful Microsoft 365 sign-ins from non-corporate IP addresses, which could indicate credential theft from users on public Wi-Fi networks as seen in the FrostArmada campaign.

indicators.name: DNS Query to Non-Standard DNS Server
indicators.pattern:
title: DNS Query to Non-Standard DNS Server
id: 8d6e2f9b-5c4a-4d8b-9e1d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects DNS queries sent to DNS servers that are not on an approved list of corporate or public resolvers. This can indicate DNS hijacking via a compromised router, as seen in the FrostArmada campaign.
references:
  - https://www.technewsworld.com/story/dns-poisoning-campaign-makes-hospitality-wi-fi-spots-inhospitable-180463.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-29
tags:
  - attack.t1557
  - attack.command_and_control
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of third-party DNS servers on misconfigured devices or by specific software.
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 53
    Protocol: 'udp'
    Image|endswith: '\svchost.exe' # Covers the DNS Client service (Dnscache)
  filter_known_dns:
    DestinationIp:
      # Add approved corporate and public DNS servers
      - '8.8.8.8'
      - '8.8.4.4'
      - '1.1.1.1'
      - '1.0.0.1'
      - '9.9.9.9'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_dns
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries to unexpected DNS servers, which can be an indicator of DNS poisoning attacks like those used in the FrostArmada campaign.
